questions.question: A solid right-circular cylinder, whose radius of the base is 15 cm and height is 12 cm, is melted and moulded into the solid right-circular cone, whose radius of the base is 24 cm. What will be the height of this cone?
questions.questionHtml: A solid right-circular cylinder, whose radius of the base is 15 cm and height is 12 cm, is melted and moulded into the solid right-circular cone, whose radius of the base is 24 cm. What will be the height of this cone?
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of the base of a cylinder (R) = 15 cm

Height (H) is 12 cm,

Radius of the base of right-circular cone (r) = 24 cm.

Formula used:

Volume of a cylinder = π × radius² × height 

Volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × r2 × h

Calcultions:

According to the question,

A solid right-circular cylinder is melted and moulded into the solid right-circular cone then

Volume of cylinder = Volume of Cone

⇒ π × (R)2 × H = (1/3) × π × r2 × h

⇒ (R)2 × H = (1/3) × r2 × h

⇒ h = ((15)2 × 12 × 3)/(24)2 

⇒ h = (225 × 36)/ 576

⇒ h = 8100/576 = 14.0625 cm

∴ The height of this cone is 14.0625 cm.

questions.question: The radius of the base of a cylinder is 14 cm and its curved surface area is 880 cm 2 . Its volume (in cm 3 ) is: \(\left(\text{Take} \ \pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\right)\)
questions.questionHtml:
The radius of the base of a cylinder is 14 cm and its curved surface area is 880 cm2. Its volume (in cm3) is:

\(\left(\text{Take} \ \pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\right)\)
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of cylinder = 14 cm

The curved surface area of the cylinder = 880 cm2

Formula used:

The curved surface area of cylinder = 2πrh

The volume of cylinder = πr2h

Where,

r = radius of the cylinder

h = height of the cylinder

Calculation:

Height of the cylinder

⇒ 2πrh = 880

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 14 × h = 880

⇒ h = 10 cm

The volume of the cylinder

⇒ (22/7) × (14)2 × 10

⇒ 6160 cm3

∴ The volume of the cylinder is 6160 cm3.

questions.question: Twelve solid hemispheres of the same size are melted and recast to in a right circular cylinder of diameter 7 cm and height 28 cm. What is the radius of the hemispheres?
questions.questionHtml: Twelve solid hemispheres of the same size are melted and recast to in a right circular cylinder of diameter 7 cm and height 28 cm. What is the radius of the hemispheres?
questions.solution:
Given:

Right circular cylinder

Diameter = 7 cm

Height = 28 cm

Formula used:

The volume of a hemisphere = \(2\over3\)πr3

The volume of a cylinder = πR2h 

Calculation:

Let the radius of the hemisphere be r cm.

Radius of the cylinder = 7/2 cm

Height of the cylinder = h = 28 cm

According to the question,

12 × The volume of a hemisphere = The volume of a cylinder 

⇒ 12 × (2/3) × π × r3 = π × R2 × h

⇒ r3 = (7 × 7 × 7)/8 = (7/2)3

⇒ r = 7/2 = 3.5 cm

questions.question: If each edge of a cube is increased by 10%, then the percentage increase in its surface area is:
questions.questionHtml: If each edge of a cube is increased by 10%, then the percentage increase in its surface area is:
questions.solution:
Formula:

If each edge of cube is increased by x%, then 

the percentage increase in its surface area = x + x + (x × x)/100

Total surface area of cube = 6a2

Calculation:

Short Trick:

∴ The percentage increase in its surface area = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 20 + 1 = 21%

Detailed Method:

Let side of cube be 10 m

Total surface area of cube = 6 × 102 = 600 m2

New side of cube = 10 × (110/100) = 11 m

New total surface area of cube = 6 × 112 = 726 m2

Area increased by = 726 - 600 = 126 m2

∴ Area increased by (in %) = (126/600) × 100 = 21%

questions.question: The surface area of a volleyball spherical is 100π cm 2 . Find the volume of air enclosed in the ball.
questions.questionHtml: The surface area of a volleyball spherical is 100π cm<sup>2</sup>. Find the volume of air enclosed in the ball.
questions.solution:
Given:

Surface area of sphere = 100π cm2

Concept Used:

Surface Area of Sphere = \(4\pi r^2\)

Volume of Sphere = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\)

Calculation:

⇒ Surface Area of spherical volleyball = 100π cm2

⇒ \(4\pi r^2=100\pi\)

⇒ \(r^2=\frac{100\pi}{4\pi}=25\)

⇒ \(r=\sqrt{25}=5\)

⇒ Now, Volume of air enclosed in the ball = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi \times 5^3=\frac{4}{3}\pi \times 125\)

⇒ Volume of air enclosed in the ball = \(\frac{500}{3}\pi\) cm3

Hence, the volume of air enclosed in the ball is \(\frac{500}{3}\pi\) cm3.

questions.question: The base of a hemispherical bowl has a circumference of 132 cm. Find the capacity of the bowl. (use π = \(\frac{22}{7}\) )

options.html: 19404 cm3
19708 cm3
16540 cm3

questions.solution:
Given:

Circumference of the base of a hemispherical bowl = 132 cm

Concept Used:

Volume of hemisphere = \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3\)

Circumference of the base of the hemisphere = \(2\pi r\)

Calculation:

⇒ Circumference of the base of hemisphere = \(2\pi r=132\)

⇒ \(2\times \frac{22}{7}\times r = 132\)

⇒ \(r=\frac{132\times 7}{44}=21\) cm

⇒ So, the capacity of hemispherical bowl = \(\frac{2}{3}\times \frac{22}{7}\times 21\times 21\times 21\)

⇒ Capacity of hemispherical bowl = \(44\times 21\times 21\) = 19404 cm3

Hence, the capacity of the bowl is 19404 cm3.

questions.question: A sphere of radius 7 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm each. How many such spheres can be made?
questions.questionHtml: A sphere of radius 7 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm each. How many such spheres can be made?
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of the large sphere, R = 7 cm

Radius of the small sphere, r = 2 cm

Concept:

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)π(radius)3

Calculation:

Volume of sphere of radius of 7 cm = n × Volume of sphere of radius 2 cm

(4/3)π(7)3 = n × (4/3)π(2)3

73 = n × 23

343 = 8n

n = 343/8 

n = 42.86

∴ The number of small spheres that can be made is 42.

questions.question: What is the height of a solid right circular cylinder whose radius is 3 cm and total surface area is 60 π cm 2 ?
questions.questionHtml: What is the height of a solid right circular cylinder whose radius is 3 cm and total surface area is 60 π cm<sup>2</sup>?
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of right circular cylinder = 3 cm.

Total surface area of cylinder = 60π cm².

Formula used:

Total surface area of cylinder = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(r + h)

Let the Height of the cylinder = h cm.

Total surface area of cylinder = 2 π r (r + h) = 60π

⇒ 2 π × 3(3 + h) = 60π

⇒ (3 + h) = 10

⇒ h = 7 cm

\(\therefore\) Height of the cylinder is 7 cm.

questions.question: Three metallic cubes whose sides are 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm respectively are melted and converted into a single cube. If there is no loss of metal in this process, then what is the length of the side of the new cube?
questions.questionHtml: Three metallic cubes whose sides are 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm respectively are melted and converted into a single cube. If there is no loss of metal in this process, then what is the length of the side of the new cube?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The total volume remains constant during the melting process.

Volume of new cube = 63 + 83 + 103

Volume = 216 + 512 + 1000 = 1728 cm3

Side of new cube = √3(1728) = 12 cm

∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: Sides of three metallic cubes are s1 = 6 cm, s2 = 8 cm, and s3 = 10 cm.

Formula Used: Volume of a cube = (side)3

⇒ Volume of 1st cube = 63 = 216 cm3

⇒ Volume of 2nd cube = 83 = 512 cm3

⇒ Volume of 3rd cube = 103 = 1000 cm3

⇒ Total volume of melted metal = 216 + 512 + 1000 = 1728 cm3

⇒ Let 'a' be the side of the new cube.

⇒ a3 = 1728

⇒ a = √3(1728)

⇒ a = 12 cm

∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.

Additional Information

Volume and Surface Area of a Cube

For a cube with side 'a', the Volume is a3 and the Total Surface Area is 6a2.

Diagonal of a Cube

The length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cube of side 'a' is given by the Diagonal formula: d = a√3.

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four vertical faces of a cube (excluding top and bottom) is called the Lateral Surface Area, which is 4a2.

questions.question: A solid metallic right circular cylinder has diameter 32 cm and height 9 cm. It is melted and recast into a solid sphere. What is the radius (in cm) of the sphere?
questions.questionHtml: A solid metallic right circular cylinder has diameter 32 cm and height 9 cm. It is melted and recast into a solid sphere. What is the radius (in cm) of the sphere?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of Cylinder = Volume of Sphere

πr2h = (4/3)πR3

16 × 16 × 9 = (4/3) × R3

R3 = 16 × 16 × 9 × 3 / 4 = 16 × 4 × 27 = 64 × 27

R = 4 × 3 = 12 cm

∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of Cylinder (d) = 32 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 16 cm

Height of Cylinder (h) = 9 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of Cylinder = πr2h

Volume of Sphere = (4/3)πR3

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of Cylinder = Volume of Sphere

⇒ π × (16)2 × 9 = (4/3) × π × R3

⇒ 256 × 9 = (4/3) × R3

⇒ R3 = (256 × 9 × 3) / 4

⇒ R3 = 64 × 27

⇒ R = ³√(64 × 27)

⇒ R = 4 × 3 = 12 cm

∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.

Additional Information

Cylinder Properties

Total Surface Area of Cylinder = 2πr(h + r) and Curved Surface Area = 2πrh.

Sphere Properties

Surface Area of Sphere = 4πR2. For a Hemisphere, Volume = (2/3)πR3 and Total Surface Area = 3πR2.

Recasting Rule

When one solid is melted and recast into another, the Volume remains constant, provided there is no wastage.

questions.question: If the radius of sphere is decreased by 10 percent, then volume of sphere will be decreased by what percentage?
questions.questionHtml: If the radius of sphere is decreased by 10 percent, then volume of sphere will be decreased by what percentage?
questions.solution:
Given:

The radius of a sphere decrease by 10%.

Concept used:

The volume of the sphere = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi {r^3}\)

Explanation:

Volume = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi {r^3}\)

If the radius decreases by 10%

r × 90% = 9r/10

New volume = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi× {(9r/10)^3}\)

(∵ \(\frac{4}{3}\pi \) is constant in both volumes so we calculated only the difference of radius basis)

Initial volume = r3

New volume = 729r3/1000

⇒ difference = r3 - 729r3/1000 = 271r3/1000

⇒ % changes = \(\frac{{271r3/1000}}{{{r^3}}} × 100\)

⇒ 27.1%

∴ The percent decrease in volume is 27.1%.

questions.question: In a right circular cylinder, the ratio of the curved surface to the total surface area is 3 ∶ 7. Find the ratio of the height of the cylinder to the radius of its base.
questions.questionHtml: In a right circular cylinder, the ratio of the curved surface to the total surface area is 3 ∶ 7. Find the ratio of the height of the cylinder to the radius of its base.
questions.solution:
Given:

Ratio of the curved surface area and total surface area of a cylinder is 3 ∶ 7.

Formula used:

Curved surface area of cylinder = 2πrh

Total surface area of cylinder = 2πrh + 2πr2

Calculation:

According to question,

Curved surface area/ Total surface area= 3/7

⇒ 2πrh/(2πrh + 2πr2) = \(\frac{3}{7}\)

⇒ 2πrh/[2πr(h + r)] = \(\frac{3}{7}\)

⇒ h/(h + r) = \(\frac{3}{7}\)

⇒ 7h = 3h + 3r

⇒ 7h - 4h = 3r

⇒ 4h = 3r

⇒ h/r = 3/4

⇒ h : r = 3 : 4

∴ The ratio of Height and Radius of a Cylinder is 3 : 4.
